title: Manantic / Menantic Creek
summary: Manantic names a neck and creek in the western part of Shelter Island. The same source notes that Shelter Island people pronounced and spelled the name locally as Menantic.
address_label: General Menantic Creek / Menantic Neck area, Shelter Island, New York
map_geometry_source: Approximate/general point for the Menantic Creek and Menantic Neck area on western Shelter Island; not an exact creek course or neck boundary.
history_content: Manantic was a traditional local name found on Shelter Island source materials and in local speech rather than as a deeply attested early legal form. Project context connects Menantic with western Shelter Island and remembered Manhanset geography, including associations with Poggatacut.
translation_content:
The source rejects the idea that Manantic means a spruce or cedar swamp. Instead, Manantic is interpreted as island creek, explained through an element for island and a tidal-stream ending, because the creek has a small island at its outlet.

Why Place Names Matter

“The naming or renaming process provides a chance to recognise the local history, culture and identity of the area.”

— City of Port Phillip, Road naming, place naming and feature naming (2026), Road naming guidance
land_loss_content: Manantic preserves a Shelter Island placename tied to creek, neck, island, and local Manhanset memory. Its survival in local pronunciation and maps shows how place names can remain in everyday geography even when early deed records are absent.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is a general point for Menantic Creek and Menantic Neck on western Shelter Island. It is intended for orientation and does not trace the creek, neck, or small island at the outlet.
